tidbit: Did you know… one story this hour was carried by two different outlets in the last few hours.
transcript:
Hourly brief, Founders' Preview. Here is what is moving in superintelligence (SI), the next generation of artificial intelligence (AI).
A former OpenAI employee has been ordered to remain in custody by a US court. Reported by NDTV: the engineer faces allegations of planting a device in the office.
Amazon has launched TorchNeuron to challenge Nvidia's dominance in artificial intelligence chips. Reported by The Tech Buzz: the new chip enables seamless PyTorch migration.
The fired OpenAI engineer accused of bugging the office has been denied release from jail. Reported by Business Insider: he will defend himself from custody.
Nscale is in talks to sell 460MW of computing power from Nvidia chips to Anthropic. Still open, per Central Oregon Daily: the deal is valued at $45 billion for artificial intelligence cloud computing.
Arkansas's attorney general has filed a lawsuit claiming the company behind ChatGPT misled users about its safety. Reported by Magnolia Banner News: the legal action targets the chatbot maker's claims.
Free every hour.
